alyssa: After onboarding a customer with sampleapp, their CI blew up with mypy errors from our autogenerated dataclasses. Minimal repro below.

alyssa: Repro:
```py
from sampleapp import GeneratedModel

m = GeneratedModel(id="1", tags=None)  # mypy: error: Argument 2 has incompatible type "None"; expected "List[str]"
```

rahul: Interestingis the generated field typed as Optional[List[str]] or List[str]?

alyssa: The generator writes Optional[List[str]] = None, but static checkers still think the init expects List[str] (probably because of kw-only or how dataclass signature is inferred).

sam: Two fixes: (A) change codegen to use default_factory=list (List[str] non-optional) and treat None at callsites as error/runtime normalize, or (B) keep Optional[List[str]] but ensure the generated __init__ signature is Optional[List[str]] and add a __post_init__ normalization.

alyssa: Prefer B so None keeps meaning "unset". Will that placate mypy/pyright?

sam: Yes, if the constructor parameter is Optional[List[str]] it won't complain. Also add typing stubs so editors don't pick up the runtime-reflected signature.

rahul: Also saw related noise around unified Client where methods sometimes show Union[SyncResult, Awaitable[SyncResult]] in editors. We should add typing-only overloads or provide AsyncClient to avoid union returns. Overloads are less invasive.

alyssa: Plan: rahul will open a PR to adjust generator to emit Optional params + __post_init__ normalizer; sam will add stub-overloads for async methods; i'll add a tiny mypy/pyright CI job to sampleapp. I'll link the repro in the PR.
